artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let T = (V, E) be a finite tournament (a directed graph in which every pair of distinct vertices is joined by exactly one arc). The dichromatic number χ⃗(T) of T is the smallest integer r such that V can be partitioned into r sets, each inducing an acyclic subtournament. For disjoint vertex subsets A, B ⊆ V, say that A dominates B if every arc between A and B is directed from A to B.

Determine whether there exists a function f : ℤ_{>0} → ℤ_{>0} with the following property: for every positive integer k and every tournament T with χ⃗(T) ≥ f(k), there exist two disjoint subsets A, B ⊆ V(T) such that A dominates B and the induced subtournaments T[A] and T[B] both satisfy χ⃗(T[A]) ≥ k and χ⃗(T[B]) ≥ k.
artifact.status_search_result: The question appears as an open problem from a recent DIGRAPHS workshop open-problems session, and related literature on tournament structure (e.g., work by Nguyen, Scott, Seymour) treats analogous "complete pair" splitting questions for the dichromatic/chromatic number as open conjectures. No published resolution was found.
